input.command:
python3 - <<'EOF'
s=open('index.html').read()
old=s[s.index('  const summerMonths'):s.index('  function avgFor')]
s=s.replace(old,'')
a=s.index('  function avgFor'); b=s.index('  const top = depths[0]')
s=s[:a]+'''  // calendar month with highest average (climatology) per depth
  function peakMonth(dep) {
    const clim = d3.rollups(valid.filter(c => c.depth === dep), v => d3.mean(v, c => c.mean), c => c.month.getUTCMonth());
    return d3.greatest(clim, d => d[1])[0];
  }
  const mName = i => d3.utcFormat("%B")(new Date(Date.UTC(2000, i, 1)));
'''+s[b:]
s=s.replace("and deep summer warming lags the surface.`","and the warmest month shifts later with depth (${mName(peakMonth(top))} at ${top} m vs ${mName(peakMonth(bot))} at ${bot} m).`")
s=s.replace("const lx = 190;","const lx = 215;")
open('index.html','w').write(s)
EOF
render index.html

content.text:
I built `index.html`: a D3 heatmap with sensor depth on the rows (2 m at the top, 40 m at the bottom) and one column per month from February 2018 to December 2025. The cell colour is the monthly mean temperature, and hatched cells mark months with no data. It renders with no errors or warnings.

The caption is calculated from the data when the page loads. It currently reads: the seasonal swing is 1.3–19.3 °C at 2 m (warmest in Sep 2025) but only 0.7–10.9 °C at 40 m. The warmest calendar month also moves later with depth: September at 2 m, October at 40 m.

```
REPORT
deliverable: index.html
requirements:
  R1: done - monthly mean of daily means per depth (d3.rollup), shown as heatmap cells
  R2: done - one column per month, Feb 2018 to Dec 2025, with year labels and quarterly month ticks
  R3: done - a depth-month with no daily rows is drawn as a hatched "no data" cell, never filled in
  R4: done - rows labelled "2 m" to "40 m", ordered by depth
  R5: done - colour legend titled "Monthly mean temperature (°C)", ticks in °C
  R6: done - title plus a one-sentence caption whose numbers are computed from the data
assumptions:
  - Monthly mean = unweighted mean of that month's daily means (not weighted by n_obs)
  - A month with at least one daily value counts as having data, so partial months are shown
  - The time range comes from the first and last dates in the data
  - Colour scale (blue to red) spans the full range of the monthly means
limitations:
  - Cells from partly covered months look the same as full months; the tooltip shows the day count
  - "Peak month by depth" in the caption is the warmest calendar month averaged over all years
  - Exact values are only shown in the hover tooltip
```
